feed.title: AI · Applied Tools — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: A hand-curated, annotated link directory across ten areas, from software and AI to security, economics and architecture. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Awesome Actions on Google
entry.summary: A resource list for Actions on Google, the developer platform for Google Assistant. Since Google shut down Conversational Actions in 2023, unlike current assistant lists it now has only historical value.

entry.title: Awesome Generative AI
entry.summary: A list of AI tools and projects that generate text, images and audio. Unlike single product pages it maps the field category by category and tracks its fast movement.

entry.title: Awesome XAI
entry.summary: A list of methods for explainable AI (XAI) — showing why a model decided as it did. Unlike general ML lists it focuses only on interpretability.

entry.title: Axiom.ai
entry.summary: Browser automation as a browser extension, with form filling, clicking and scraping steps assembled by drag and drop. Against Puppeteer or Playwright it runs inside your own session, so pages you are already logged into need no separate authentication.

entry.title: Browse AI
entry.summary: Extracts data from websites and monitors them for changes without code — you train it by clicking in the browser. Against frameworks like Scrapy there are no selectors to write, and it attempts to self-heal when a page layout shifts.

entry.title: LibreTranslate
entry.summary: A self-hostable machine translation API running Argos Translate models. Against the Google Translate API the text never leaves your server and there is no per-request charge — lower quality, higher privacy.

entry.title: ResuMax
entry.summary: Tailors a résumé to a specific posting and watches the formatting ATS parsers need. Unlike general writing assistants, it focuses on matching the résumé to the posting.

entry.title: Ada Health
entry.summary: Narrows symptoms through a structured question flow and ranks possible causes; CE-marked as a medical device. Unlike searching symptoms online it is disciplined: ordered questions instead of random pages, and causes ranked by likelihood.

entry.title: Aider
entry.summary: Runs in the terminal and writes each change as its own git commit. Unlike editor-based assistants it gives you that safety net: revert a step you dislike with `git revert`.

entry.title: AlphaFold Server
entry.summary: Predicts structures of protein, DNA and ligand complexes with AlphaFold 3. Unlike ColabFold it needs no install or GPU and runs AlphaFold 3; in exchange, daily jobs are capped and commercial use is restricted.

entry.title: AskYourPDF
entry.summary: Collects many documents into one library you can query together, with page-cited answers. That is where it parts from single-file tools.

entry.title: AutoGluon
entry.summary: Three lines gives a strong baseline on tabular data. Unlike training a single model, it trains several and combines them by stacking; frequently used as a Kaggle baseline.

entry.title: BioGPT
entry.summary: A language model trained on PubMed abstracts, more accurate than general models at tasks like drug–disease relation extraction. Built for information extraction rather than generation.

entry.title: Blackbox AI
entry.summary: Merges snippet search with chat. Unlike general chatbots, it searches repositories and docs and uses the hits as context.

entry.title: Bolt.new
entry.summary: Runs Node.js in the browser via WebContainers, so the generated full-stack app previews instantly without a server round trip. Unlike component generators such as v0 it runs the whole app, and errors are fixed in place.

entry.title: Buffer AI Assistant
entry.summary: Lives inside the scheduling tool, repackaging one post for each platform’s tone and length — removing the round trip to a separate copy tool.

entry.title: ChatPDF
entry.summary: A tool for asking questions of a PDF — upload and start without signing up. Unlike tools such as Humata it has the lowest friction; in exchange there is no library management or multi-document support.

entry.title: ChemCrow
entry.summary: An LLM agent that operates chemistry tools — RDKit, reaction databases, synthesis planners. Consulting real computation instead of the model’s recall sharply lowers error in chemistry.

entry.title: Cline
entry.summary: A coding agent that creates files and runs commands inside VS Code, asking approval for each action. Unlike fully autonomous agents, that slowing step gives back the oversight you would otherwise lose.

entry.title: CodeGeeX
entry.summary: An open code model and plugin with a Chinese interface and regional infrastructure — a working alternative where access to Western services is limited.

entry.title: ColabFold
entry.summary: Speeds up sequence alignment with MMseqs2 to make AlphaFold runnable in Colab. Unlike AlphaFold Server, you can batch-process your own sequences without hitting a quota.

entry.title: Consensus
entry.summary: Summarises which way the literature leans on a question and shows the ratio of supporting to contradicting studies. Finding one paper and seeing the field’s tendency are different jobs.

entry.title: Continue
entry.summary: An open-source coding assistant for VS Code and JetBrains, where you pick which model does completion and which does chat. Unlike GitHub Copilot the model choice is open — point it at a local model and code never leaves your machine.

entry.title: Cursor
entry.summary: A VS Code fork that indexes your codebase and makes multi-file editing the primary flow. Unlike a plugin it proposes changes as diffs and waits for approval.

entry.title: DeepChem
entry.summary: A machine-learning library for drug discovery, including molecular featurisation and dataset loaders. Unlike general ML libraries, it takes on the tedious part of getting chemical data model-ready.

entry.title: DeepL Write
entry.summary: Rewrites the sentence and offers tone variants instead of flagging errors. Grammarly corrects, this rewrites — two different jobs.

entry.title: Elicit
entry.summary: Screens hundreds of papers and extracts fields such as sample size, method and finding into a table. Unlike general chat assistants, it is built for the screening step that eats the most time in a systematic review.

entry.title: Explainpaper
entry.summary: Simplifies whichever passage you highlight in a PDF. Unlike tools that summarise the whole document, it opens up only the one place you got stuck — which makes it narrow but accurate.

entry.title: FinGPT
entry.summary: Open models and data pipelines for financial text, including fine-tunes for sentiment and news classification. An open research alternative to a Bloomberg terminal.

entry.title: Fireflies.ai
entry.summary: Extracts decisions, action items and questions rather than a raw transcript, and can write into a CRM. Otter concentrates on transcription; this on extraction.

entry.title: GitHub Copilot
entry.summary: In-editor completion and chat. Unlike its rivals it is strong on governance: in the enterprise plan, whether code is sent to a model and which models are allowed can be managed as policy.

entry.title: Google Colab
entry.summary: Jupyter in the browser with a free T4 GPU. Unlike local Jupyter it needs no setup or hardware; in exchange sessions are time-limited and files vanish when the machine recycles, so long training runs need Drive mounted.

entry.title: Grammarly
entry.summary: English grammar and style checking through an extension that follows you everywhere you type. Unlike LanguageTool its style and tone suggestions are stronger; there is no Turkish support, so it only makes sense for English.

entry.title: H2O.ai
entry.summary: A distributed AutoML platform. Unlike library-only solutions, it also brings explainability and productionisation tooling, and can spill out of memory on large datasets.

entry.title: HubSpot Campaign Assistant
entry.summary: Generates email, landing page and ad copy against a campaign goal, free and without requiring a HubSpot account.

entry.title: Humata
entry.summary: A PDF assistant aimed at comparative reading of long technical documents. Unlike quick tools such as ChatPDF, each answer carries a source-page link so you can verify the claim in the document.

entry.title: Julius AI
entry.summary: Upload a CSV or Excel and analyse by chatting; it runs Python behind the scenes and produces charts. Unlike general chatbots it shows the code it used — which is what makes the result verifiable.

entry.title: Kaggle Notebooks
entry.summary: Notebooks sitting on the same platform as the datasets, with a weekly GPU quota more predictable than Colab’s. The real value is being able to read other people’s solutions.

entry.title: KNIME
entry.summary: A node-based visual analytics platform where the whole pipeline is saved and re-runnable. Unlike Python scripts it delivers reproducibility without writing code; common in enterprise data teams.

entry.title: LanguageTool
entry.summary: Rule-based checking for 30+ languages including Turkish. Unlike Grammarly it supports Turkish and can be self-hosted — the only real option when the text must not go to a company.
